title: Improving Iterative Ptychographic Reconstructions with Generative Neural Networks
content: Electron ptychography is a powerful technique that utilizes four-dimensional scanning transmission electron microscopy (4DSTEM) to perform high-resolution, dose-efficient imaging of material and biological samples [1]. Conventional iterative ptychographic reconstruction techniques, such as those based on gradient descent, are popular because they can simultaneously reconstruct the sample object and the electron probe [2]. This leads to several benefits, including super resolution by removing probe aberrations, multislice ptychography which can provide information about the sample along the beam direction, and the ability to add regularization for correcting experimental inaccuracies such as scan position error. The downside of iterative techniques is that they are computationally expensive and can be difficult to implement due to the many hyperparameters that must be optimized. Machine learning (ML) methods are a potential solution to these problems, as algorithms that utilize generative neural networks have been successfully applied to a wide range of inverse problems. Deep image priors (DIPs) are one such example, which apply the regularizing architecture of a convolutional neural network (CNN) to generate noise-resistant reconstructions [3, 4]. In this work, we present a DIP-enabled method for performing ptychographic reconstructions that can more robustly and accurately reconstruct ptychographic data than conventional methods.
